## 2. Page Anatomy

A global header floats over the hero. The page body has **6 sections**:

| # | Section | Anchor id | Background | Data source |
|---|---------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| 0 | Site Header (global, floating) | ΓÇö | white pill over hero | static nav config + auth state |
| 1 | Hero | `home` | campus photo + white gradient | static |
| 2 | Platform Highlights | `about` | white card overlapping hero | static config |
| 3 | Featured & Upcoming Activities | `activities` | page background (white/very light) | **API** |
| 4 | HCMUS Services (Quick Access) | `services` | full-bleed deep blue | static config + **auth state** |
| 5 | Help / Guide | `help` | white with decorative blue circles | static config |
| 6 | Footer | `contact` | full-bleed deep blue | static config |

Header nav items map to anchors: Home ΓåÆ `#home`, About Us ΓåÆ `#about`, Activities ΓåÆ `#activities`, Services ΓåÆ `#services`, Help ΓåÆ `#help`.

---

## 3. Fit with the Existing Frontend

Existing structure (Next.js App Router): `app/(public)`, `app/(protected)/{admin,organizer,student}`, `features/auth/*` (context, provider, schema, services + mock service, types, DTO), `hooks/useAuth.ts`, `libs/{api-client,navigation,roles,session}.ts`, `components/{forms,icons}`, `types/{api,entities}.ts`.

Follow the same conventions already used by `features/auth`:
- Feature-first folders under `features/<name>/`.
- **Service + mock service** pair behind one interface (see `auth.service.ts` / `mock.auth.service.ts`). Reuse whatever switching mechanism auth uses (env flag or factory) ΓÇö do not invent a second one.
- **DTO vs domain type separation** (`*.dto.ts` = wire format, `*.ts` = UI model) with a mapper.
- One icon per file in `components/icons`.
- HTTP goes through `libs/api-client.ts` only; no raw `fetch` in components.
- Role ΓåÆ dashboard resolution uses `libs/roles.ts` / `libs/navigation.ts`. If a `getDashboardPath(role)` helper does not exist yet, add it there (do not hardcode paths in components).

### 3.1 Routing

- Landing route: **`app/(public)/page.tsx`** ΓåÆ renders `<LandingPage />` from `features/landing`.
- **Remove or empty the current `app/page.tsx`** ΓÇö two files resolving to `/` conflict.
- `app/(public)/layout.tsx` currently serves `/login`; check what it renders. The landing page composes `SiteHeader` / `SiteFooter` itself (inside `LandingPage`) so `/login` is not affected. If more marketing pages appear later, extract a `(site)` route group with a shared layout.
- The landing page is **always accessible**, including for authenticated users (no auto-redirect to dashboard). Authenticated users get a "Dashboard" button in the header and unlocked services.

### 3.2 Rendering strategy

- `app/(public)/page.tsx` is a **Server Component** (static shell, SEO metadata).
- Interactive/stateful parts are Client Components (`"use client"`): `SiteHeader` (auth state, mobile menu, scroll-spy), `ActivitiesSection` (data fetch states), `ServicesSection` (auth gating).
- Activities are fetched **client-side** through a hook so a slow/failed API never blocks the page. [ASSUMPTION] If the project already uses React Query/SWR in `providers/provider.tsx`, use it inside the hook instead of hand-rolled state; the hook's return contract stays the same.

---

## 4. File / Folder Plan

## 6. Shared Reusable Components (contracts)

`SurfaceCard` = white rounded container with `--shadow-card`; used by Highlights wrapper, ActivityCard, GuideCard (with `gradient` prop).

---

## 7. Section Specifications

### 7.0 Site Header (global)

**UI**
- Floating white pill, horizontally centered, Γëê `24px` from top, width Γëê container width, height Γëê `56px`, soft shadow, `position: fixed/sticky`, `z-index` above hero.
- Left: `Logo` ΓÇö "my" in gold serif/italic + "HCMUS" in bold primary blue. Links to `/`.

- Auth-dependent right-side control (`useAuth()` ΓåÆ `{ user, isAuthenticated, isLoading }`):
  - `isLoading` ΓåÆ render a fixed-width skeleton in place of the button (no layout shift).
  - Guest ΓåÆ **Log In** ΓåÆ `/login`.
  - Authenticated ΓåÆ **Dashboard** button ΓåÆ `getDashboardPath(user.role)` (+ optional avatar/menu with Logout; reuse existing logout from `useAuth`).

### 7.1 Hero (`#home`)

**UI**
- Full-width section, min-height Γëê `540ΓÇô600px` (design Γëê `540px` visible before highlights card overlaps).
- Background: campus building photo (`next/image`, `fill`, `priority`, `object-fit: cover`) with a **white gradient overlay** fading the photo into the page background on the left and bottom (gradient from `rgba(255,255,255,.9)` at left/bottom to transparent at right/top).   - **Subtitle** (Γëê `18px`, regular, dark text): "A platform for the extracurricular activities and student training scores." (wraps in 2 lines).
  - **CTA row** (gap Γëê `12px`):
    - `Get Started` ΓÇö `Button variant="white" size="lg"`, pill, primary-blue bold text, soft shadow.
    - `Explore the activities` ΓÇö `Button variant="primary" size="lg"`, pill. (Design typo "activites" ΓåÆ use **"activities"**.)

**Behavior / flow**

  - Right (max-width Γëê `340px`, muted, 12ΓÇô13px, aligned to the right half): "Bring activities, participation, training scores, and essential campus services together in one place, making student life easier to manage and stay connected."
- Below: **3-column grid** of `FeatureCard` (gap Γëê `40px`). Each card:
  - Image (Γëê `16:9`-ish, Γëê `205├ù105` in design, small radius `4ΓÇô8px`, `object-fit: cover`).

  - Description (Γëê `12ΓÇô13px`, muted, 3 lines).

  1. **Discover & Join Activities** ΓÇö "Discover extracurricular activities, register for opportunities, and manage your participation with ease."
  2. **Track Your Student Journey** ΓÇö "Keep track of your activities, attendance, training scores, and academic schedule in one place."

**Behavior**

### 7.3 Featured & Upcoming Activities (`#activities`) ΓÇö API-driven

**UI (data present)**

  2. Title ΓÇö UPPERCASE as provided by data, bold Γëê `14px`, clamp to **4 lines** (`line-clamp-4`) with ellipsis.

- **`ActivityCard variant="compact"`** (horizontal): thumbnail left (Γëê `100├ù80`, rounded), right: title (bold Γëê `12px`, uppercase as provided, clamp **3 lines**), category tag (italic/muted), date-time, location. No status row in the compact design.
- The second featured card in the PNG is a **design placeholder** showing labels "Key Tags / TIME / Location / Registration Status: Open/Closed/Upcoming" ΓÇö it documents the *possible values*, not a different layout. Render it identically to the first featured card with real data.

**Data contract**

```ts
// features/activities/types/activity.dto.ts  (wire format ΓÇô adjust to backend)

  title: string;
  image_url: string | null;

Index: src/client/specs/001-landing-page/tasks.md
===================================================================
--- src/client/specs/001-landing-page/tasks.md	
+++ src/client/specs/001-landing-page/tasks.md	
@@ -1,365 +1,365 @@
 # Tasks: Public Landing Page
 
 **Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-landing-page/`
 
 **Prerequisites**: `plan.md`, `spec.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/`, `quickstart.md`
 
 **Tests**: Included because the implementation plan and source specification explicitly require deterministic verification of formatting, mapping, activity states, service gating, grid behavior, navigation, and accessibility. Test tasks precede the implementation they validate where practical.
 
 **Organization**: The user requested five logical phases. This list preserves those phases while using user-story phases for independent delivery slices. Phase 1 and Phase 2 are shared foundation; Phases 3-7 are user stories in priority order; Phase 8 is integration; Phase 9 is quality assurance. All paths are relative to `src/client`.
 
 ## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`
 
 - **[P]**: Can run in parallel with other [P] tasks in the same phase; different files and no incomplete dependency.
 - **[Story]**: `[US1]` through `[US5]`, matching `spec.md`.
 - Every task includes an exact file path and a verification or acceptance condition.
 
 ## Path Conventions
 
 - Single Next.js application rooted at `src/client`.
 - Application code: `src/`.
 - Shared test harness: `tests/`.
 - Feature code: `src/features/<feature>/`.
 - Static assets: `public/images/`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Phase 1: Project and Shared Foundation
 
 **Purpose**: Establish test tooling, shared contracts, tokens, utilities, and the auth-state prerequisite used by all stories.
 
-- [ ] T001 Add development-only test tooling and scripts to `package.json`: `vitest`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `jsdom`, `vite-tsconfig-paths`, `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/jest-dom`, `@testing-library/user-event`, `axe-core`; add `"test": "vitest run"` and `"test:watch": "vitest"`. Verify `npm install` succeeds and `npm test -- --passWithNoTests` runs. Covers plan Testing Strategy.
-- [ ] T002 [P] Create `vitest.config.ts` with the React plugin, `jsdom` environment, `vite-tsconfig-paths`, `tests/setup.ts`, and test-file patterns. Verify `npm test -- --passWithNoTests` loads the config. Covers plan Testing Strategy.
-- [ ] T003 [P] Create `tests/setup.ts` with jest-dom matchers and jsdom shims for `matchMedia`, `IntersectionObserver`, `scrollIntoView`, `HTMLDialogElement.showModal`, and `HTMLDialogElement.close`; add shared mocks for `next/image` and `next/navigation` only where required. Verify a trivial render test passes. Covers plan Testing Strategy.
-- [ ] T004 [P] Create `tests/test-utils.tsx` with a typed render helper and `expectNoA11yViolations` using `axe-core`. Verify the helper can render a simple component without importing feature internals. Covers FR-063 through FR-070 and SC-008.
-- [ ] T005 [P] Create `src/types/navigation.ts` with `SectionId` (`home`, `about`, `activities`, `services`, `help`, `contact`) and `NavigationLink` (`id`, `label`, `href: \`#${SectionId}\``); create `src/types/site.ts` with `FooterContent` (`brandDescription`, `contactHeading`, `address`, `phones`, `email`, `quickLinksHeading`, `quickLinks`). Verify `tsc` accepts the shapes from `data-model.md`. Covers FR-003, FR-054, and FR-072.

 ## Dependencies and Execution Order
 
 ### Phase Dependencies
 
 - **Phase 1**: No dependencies; start immediately.
 - **Phase 2**: Depends on Phase 1 tokens/types; blocks landing composition.
 - **Phase 3 (US1)**: Depends on Phase 1 and Phase 2; delivers the MVP shell, grouped activity success, and all six section shells.
 - **Phase 4 (US2)**: Depends on US1 activity types/services; can begin once the US1 activity success path exists.
 - **Phase 5 (US3)**: Depends on US1 services shell and Phase 1 auth memo fix; can run in parallel with US2 if staffed.
 - **Phase 6 (US4)**: Depends on US1 header/hero/services and Phase 1 navigation helpers; can run in parallel with US2/US3 after US1.
 - **Phase 7 (US5)**: Depends on US1 header/hero and Phase 1 navigation helpers; can run in parallel with US2/US3/US4 after US1.
 - **Phase 8**: Depends on all desired user stories.
 - **Phase 9**: Depends on Phase 8.
 
 ### User Story Dependencies
 
 - **US1 (P1)**: No dependency on other stories; MVP.
 - **US2 (P2)**: Uses US1 activity types and success path; independently testable across outcomes.
 - **US3 (P3)**: Uses US1 services shell and shared auth state; independently testable for gating.
 - **US4 (P4)**: Uses US1 header/hero/services and shared auth state; independently testable for roles.
 - **US5 (P5)**: Uses US1 header/hero; independently testable for navigation.
 
 ### Within Each Story
 
 - Write the listed tests first and confirm the expected failure before implementation.
 - Types and config before services/components.
 - Services and mappers before hooks.
 - Primitive cards before grids/sections.
 - Integrate only through public feature barrels.
 - Do not modify backend code, API routes, or the proxy for this feature.
 
 ### Parallel Opportunities
 
 - Phase 1 test harness tasks T002-T004 are parallel after T001.
 - Phase 1 shared utilities T009-T016 are largely parallel by file, except T010 depends on T009 and T012 depends on T011.
 - Phase 2 primitives T017-T024 are parallel by file.
 - US1 config tasks T028-T030 are parallel; T038 can run alongside them.
 - US1 activity presentation T046-T047 can run in parallel after activity types.
 - US2 tests T051-T056 are parallel; implementation T058, T059, and T062 can run alongside mapper work.
 - US3 tests T069-T070 are parallel; config/icons T071/T074 can run before card/section gating.
 - US4 test tasks T077-T078 are parallel; header/hero/services updates T079-T081 touch different files.
 - US5 tests T084-T085 are parallel; scroll utilities and login redirect can be developed alongside header work once tests exist.
 - Phase 8 checks T095-T102 are independent verification tasks and can be assigned to different reviewers.
 - Phase 9 manual checks T106-T112 can run in parallel by different reviewers, while T103-T105 are sequential quality gates.

 ## Implementation Strategy
 
 ### MVP First
 
 1. Complete Phase 1 and Phase 2.
 2. Complete US1 (Phase 3) to deliver the public shell, all six sections, grouped activity success, and guest orientation.
 3. Stop and validate US1 with `quickstart.md` sections 1, 2, and 5.
 4. Deploy/demo the MVP before adding outcome, gating, role, and navigation refinements.
 
 ### Incremental Delivery
 
 1. Foundation + primitives ΓåÆ landing shell.
 2. US2 ΓåÆ trustworthy activity outcomes.
 3. US3 ΓåÆ services conversion path.
 4. US4 ΓåÆ signed-in continuity.
 5. US5 ΓåÆ navigation and mobile polish.
 6. Integration and QA ΓåÆ release candidate.
 
 ### Parallel Team Strategy
 
 After US1, assign US2 (activity outcomes), US3 (services), US4 (roles), and US5 (navigation) to separate developers. US2/US3 touch activity/services files; US4/US5 touch header/hero/navigation files. Coordinate shared files (`SiteHeader.tsx`, `HeroActions.tsx`, `ServicesSection.tsx`, `LandingPage.tsx`) through one owner per file.

 - [P] tasks are safe to run in parallel only when they touch different files and their listed dependencies are complete.
 - Tests are required by the plan/source specification; run them before marking the paired implementation complete.
 - Every user story is independently demoable at its checkpoint.
 - Do not add runtime dependencies; test dependencies are dev-only and justified in `plan.md`.
 - Do not modify backend code, API routes, or the existing proxy for this feature.
 - Pending product inputs remain configurable: two service names/icons, hero headline wording, help destinations, footer copy, and the confirmed activity contract/image host.

**Checkpoint**: The integrated page satisfies the cross-section behavior and boundary rules.

## Phase 9: Quality Assurance and Polish

**Purpose**: Validate responsive behavior, accessibility, type safety, linting, visual consistency, and release readiness.

- [ ] T103 Run `npm run lint` from `package.json` and fix all new errors/warnings in `src/features/landing/`, `src/features/activities/`, `src/components/ui/`, `src/components/layout/`, and auth-adjacent changes. Verify the command exits cleanly. Covers constitution quality gates.

## Dependencies and Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Phase 1**: No dependencies; start immediately.
- **Phase 2**: Depends on Phase 1 tokens/types; blocks landing composition.
- **Phase 3 (US1)**: Depends on Phase 1 and Phase 2; delivers the MVP shell, grouped activity success, and all six section shells.
- **Phase 4 (US2)**: Depends on US1 activity types/services; can begin once the US1 activity success path exists.
- **Phase 5 (US3)**: Depends on US1 services shell and Phase 1 auth memo fix; can run in parallel with US2 if staffed.
- **Phase 6 (US4)**: Depends on US1 header/hero/services and Phase 1 navigation helpers; can run in parallel with US2/US3 after US1.
- **Phase 7 (US5)**: Depends on US1 header/hero and Phase 1 navigation helpers; can run in parallel with US2/US3/US4 after US1.
- **Phase 8**: Depends on all desired user stories.
- **Phase 9**: Depends on Phase 8.

### User Story Dependencies

- **US1 (P1)**: No dependency on other stories; MVP.
- **US2 (P2)**: Uses US1 activity types and success path; independently testable across outcomes.
- **US3 (P3)**: Uses US1 services shell and shared auth state; independently testable for gating.
- **US4 (P4)**: Uses US1 header/hero/services and shared auth state; independently testable for roles.
- **US5 (P5)**: Uses US1 header/hero; independently testable for navigation.

### Within Each Story

- Write the listed tests first and confirm the expected failure before implementation.
- Types and config before services/components.
- Services and mappers before hooks.
- Primitive cards before grids/sections.
- Integrate only through public feature barrels.
- Do not modify backend code, API routes, or the proxy for this feature.

### Parallel Opportunities

- Phase 1 test harness tasks T002-T004 are parallel after T001.
- Phase 1 shared utilities T009-T016 are largely parallel by file, except T010 depends on T009 and T012 depends on T011.
- Phase 2 primitives T017-T024 are parallel by file.
- US1 config tasks T028-T030 are parallel; T038 can run alongside them.
- US1 activity presentation T046-T047 can run in parallel after activity types.
- US2 tests T051-T056 are parallel; implementation T058, T059, and T062 can run alongside mapper work.
- US3 tests T069-T070 are parallel; config/icons T071/T074 can run before card/section gating.
- US4 test tasks T077-T078 are parallel; header/hero/services updates T079-T081 touch different files.
- US5 tests T084-T085 are parallel; scroll utilities and login redirect can be developed alongside header work once tests exist.
- Phase 8 checks T095-T102 are independent verification tasks and can be assigned to different reviewers.
- Phase 9 manual checks T106-T112 can run in parallel by different reviewers, while T103-T105 are sequential quality gates.

- **US4 (P4)**: Uses US1 header/hero/services and shared auth state; independently testable for roles.
- **US5 (P5)**: Uses US1 header/hero; independently testable for navigation.

- Types and config before services/components.
- Services and mappers before hooks.
- Primitive cards before grids/sections.

This is a spec contradiction: T041 route exports metadata from config/seo.ts but T040/T095 say no route imports internal folder. The "Feature public APIs exports only LandingPage" and "SEO values live in config" can be resolved by route importing config? Could move metadata to a shared `src/libs/seo` but then not config. Could have `LandingPage` server component not export metadata. Hmm.

Maybe the intended interpretation: routes may import config (configuration) but not component internals? But T095 says internal folders. Config is internal. T041 explicitly says route exports metadata from config/seo.ts. Likely T095 should be interpreted as routes/shared layout/sibling features not import another feature's component/service internals; config direct is an accepted exception for route metadata. Yet it says "never". We should either fix by exporting metadata through a route-local file that re-exports config? Still route imports local file, and local file imports feature config. That just moves violation.
Could create `src/app/(public)/metadata.ts` that imports feature config. Still route doesn't import feature internal; but same layer. T095 says routes, shared layout, sibling features; `src/app/(public)/metadata.ts` is route-adjacent, still app. Not ideal.

Then barrel still only LandingPage, route imports `@/features/landing/public-metadata`. But feature root file is outside internal folders? It's within feature but not `config/`. "feature internals" means components/services; config is maybe internal too. Not a clear win. Alternatively add `export const metadata` in route with literal values and then T097 fails. I think direct config import is acceptable per T041 explicit instruction. We can note T095 partial due documented conflict, not mark complete. Good.

Need not resolve contradiction now unless user expects. Better document as known spec conflict, but no user input needed? It's a decision. Could ask? We have autonomy. But tasks say no route internal import and metadata from config. We can satisfy both by adding a new public API module at feature root specifically for route metadata? But "landing index exports only LandingPage" unchanged. Example:
`src/features/landing/metadata.ts`:
```
export { LANDING_METADATA } from "./config/seo";
```
Route imports `@/features/landing/metadata`. This is a feature entry point, but not barrel? Still route imports feature file not internal folder. The constitution says route stays thin, no direct cross-feature internals. Metadata module is public-ish. However T095 says "routes ... never import another feature's internal folders" - `metadata.ts` is not a folder. This satisfies literal. But is it overengineering? It also creates another feature public API beyond only LandingPage, though T095 only mentions index exports. Acceptable. But we can also re-export metadata from index, but no. I think this is a reasonable fix. Add `features/landing/metadata.ts`, route import. Then T095 passes literal. But T097 still. Good. Do it.

Also `SiteHeader` is shared layout receiving nav. Good.

Other cross-feature imports? LandingPage imports ActivitiesSection via barrel? Let's verify.

"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { useAuth } from "@/hooks/useAuth";
import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import type { LoginSchemaType } from "@/features/auth/schema/login.schema";
import { LoginSchema } from "@/features/auth/schema/login.schema";
import { SubmitHandler, useForm, useWatch } from "react-hook-form";
import { zodResolver } from "@hookform/resolvers/zod";
import { UserIcon } from "../icons/UserIcon";
import { UsersIcon } from "../icons/UsersIcon";
import { LoginRequest } from "@/features/auth/types/auth.dto";
import { getDashboardPath, isSafeRedirectPath } from "@/libs/navigation";

type LoginFormProps = {
    redirectTo?: string;
};

const ROLE_OPTIONS = [
    {
        value: "student",
        label: "Student",
        icon: "user",
    },
    {
        value: "organizer",
        label: "Organizer",
        icon: "users",
    },
] as const;




function LoginForm({ redirectTo }: LoginFormProps) {
    const router = useRouter();
    const authContext = useAuth();
    const [loginError, setLoginError] = useState<string | null>(null);

    const form = useForm<LoginSchemaType>({
        resolver: zodResolver(LoginSchema),
        defaultValues: {
            role: 'student',
            email: '',
            password: '',
        },
    })

    const role = useWatch({
        control: form.control,
        name: 'role',
        defaultValue: 'student',
    })

    const email = useWatch({
        control: form.control,
        name: 'email',
        defaultValue: '',
    });

    const password = useWatch({
        control: form.control,
        name: 'password',
        defaultValue: '',
    });
    const isDisabled = !email || !password || form.formState.isSubmitting;

    const onSubmit: SubmitHandler<LoginSchemaType> = async (data: LoginRequest) => {
        setLoginError(null);

        try {
            const user = await authContext.login(data);

            if (user) {
                const destination =
                    redirectTo && isSafeRedirectPath(redirectTo)
                        ? redirectTo
                        : getDashboardPath(user.role);
                router.replace(destination);
            }
            else {
                setLoginError("Login failed. Please check your credentials.");
            }
        }
        catch (error) {
            // Placeholder for later error handling
            console.error("Login failed", error);
            setLoginError(
                error instanceof Error
                    ? error.message
                    : "Login failed. Please check your credentials."
            );
        }
    }

    return (
        <form
            onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)}
            className="w-full"
        >
            {/* Role selection */}
            <div className="mb-5">
                <p className="mb-3 text-xl font-medium text-[#10132f]">
                    Select user type
                </p>

                <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-5">
                    {ROLE_OPTIONS.map((option) => {
                        const isSelected = role === option.value;

                        return (
                            <button
                                key={option.value}
                                type="button"
                                aria-pressed={isSelected}
                                onClick={() => {
                                    form.setValue("role", option.value, {
                                        shouldValidate: true,
                                        shouldDirty: true,
                                    });
                                }}
                                className={`
                                    flex h-[53px] items-center justify-center
                                    gap-3 rounded-lg border-2 px-3
                                    text-xl font-semibold transition-colors
                                    ${isSelected
                                        ? "border-[#1b4da5] text-[#1b4da5]"
                                        : "border-[#b5b5b5] text-[#aaa] hover:border-[#1b4da5] hover:text-[#1b4da5]"
                                    }
                                `}
                            >
                                {option.icon === "user"
                                    ? <UserIcon />
                                    : <UsersIcon />
                                }

                                {option.label}
                            </button>
                        );
                    })}
                </div>
            </div>

            {/* Email */}
            <div className="mb-5">
                <label
                    htmlFor="email"
                    className="mb-2 block text-xl text-[#10132f]"
                >
                    Email address
                </label>

                <input
                    id="email"
                    type="email"
                    autoComplete="email"
                    placeholder="Enter your email..."
                    {...form.register("email")}
                    className="
                        h-[58px] w-full rounded-2xl border-2
                        border-[#b5b5b5] bg-white px-5
                        text-base text-[#10132f]
                        outline-none transition-colors
                        placeholder:text-[#aaa]
                        focus:border-[#1b4da5]
                    "
                />

                {form.formState.errors.email && (
                    <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-red-500">
                        {form.formState.errors.email.message}
                    </p>
                )}
            </div>

            {/* Password */}
            <div className="mb-3">
                <label
                    htmlFor="password"
                    className="mb-2 block text-xl text-[#10132f]"
                >
                    Password
                </label>

                <input
                    id="password"
                    type="password"
                    autoComplete="current-password"
                    placeholder="Enter your password..."
                    {...form.register("password")}
                    className="
                        h-[58px] w-full rounded-2xl border-2
                        border-[#b5b5b5] bg-white px-5
                        text-base text-[#10132f]
                        outline-none transition-colors
                        placeholder:text-[#aaa]
                        focus:border-[#1b4da5]
                    "
                />

                {form.formState.errors.password && (
                    <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-red-500">
                        {form.formState.errors.password.message}
                    </p>
                )}
            </div>

            {/* Forgot password */}
            <div className="mb-2 text-right">
                <a
                    href="/forgot-password"
                    className="text-base text-[#929292] hover:text-[#1b4da5]"
                >
                    Forgot Password?
                </a>
            </div>

            {/* Login error */}
            {loginError && (
                <p
                    role="alert"
                    className="mb-3 rounded-lg bg-red-50 p-3 text-sm text-red-600"
                >
                    {loginError}
                </p>
            )}

            {/* Submit */}
            <button
                type="submit"
                disabled={isDisabled}
                className="
                    h-[53px] w-full rounded-2xl
                    bg-[#1b4da5] text-xl font-medium text-white
                    shadow-md transition-colors
                    hover:bg-[#153e89]
                    active:scale-[0.99]
                    disabled:cursor-not-allowed
                    disabled:opacity-50
                "
            >
                {form.formState.isSubmitting
                    ? "Logging in..."
                    : "Log In"
                }
            </button>

            {/* Social login placeholder */}
            <div className="mt-7 border-t border-[#d5d5d5] pt-6">
                <p className="text-center text-sm text-[#999]">
                    Other sign-in methods
                </p>
                <div className="mt-4 flex justify-center gap-6">
                    <button
                        type="button"
                        disabled
                        aria-label="Google sign-in coming soon"
                        className="cursor-not-allowed opacity-40"
                    >
                        <span className="text-3xl font-bold text-[#4285F4]">
                            G
                        </span>
                    </button>

                    <button
                        type="button"
                        disabled
                        aria-label="Microsoft sign-in coming soon"
                        className="cursor-not-allowed"
                    >
                        <span className="grid h-7 w-7 grid-cols-2 gap-[2px]">
                            <span className="bg-[#f25022]" />
                            <span className="bg-[#7fba00]" />
                            <span className="bg-[#00a4ef]" />
                            <span className="bg-[#ffb900]" />
                        </span>
                    </button>
                </div>
            </div>
        </form>
    );
}
export default LoginForm;   
import LoginForm from "@/components/forms/LoginForm";

type LoginPageProps = {
  searchParams: Promise<{
    redirectTo?: string | string[];
  }>;
};

async function LoginPage({ searchParams }: LoginPageProps) {

  const redirectTo = Array.isArray(params.redirectTo)
    ? params.redirectTo[0]
    : params.redirectTo;

  return (
    <main className="
            relative grid min-h-screen
            grid-cols-1 bg-[#f8f8f8]
            lg:grid-cols-[60%_40%]
        ">
      <div
        aria-hidden="true"
        className="
                    pointer-events-none absolute inset-y-0 right-0
                    hidden w-[45%] bg-cover bg-center
                    lg:block
                    bg-[url('/images/hcmus-campus.png')]
                "
      >
        <div className="
                    absolute inset-0
                    bg-gradient-to-r
                    from-[#f8f8f8] via-[#f8f8f8]/50 to-transparent
                " />
        <div className="
                    absolute inset-0
                    bg-gradient-to-t
                    from-[#f8f8f8]/50 via-transparent to-transparent
                " />
      </div>

      <section className="
                relative z-10 flex min-h-screen
                flex-col items-center
                px-6 pb-10 pt-7
                lg:col-start-1">
        <Link
          href="/"
          aria-label="Back to home"
          className="
                        absolute left-2 top-2
                        flex h-9 w-16 items-center justify-center
                        rounded-full bg-[#1b4da5] text-white
                        transition-colors hover:bg-[#153e89]
                    "
        >
          <svg
            viewBox="0 0 24 24"
            fill="none"
            stroke="currentColor"
            strokeWidth="1.8"
            className="h-6 w-6"
            aria-hidden="true"
          >
            <path d="M19 12H5M12 19l-7-7 7-7" />
          </svg>
        </Link>

        <header className="mb-15 mt-10 text-center">
          <Image
            src="/images/logo.svg"
            alt="myHCMUS Logo"
            width={180}
            height={45}
            priority
            className="mx-auto h-auto w-[200px]"
          />

          <p className="mt-1 text-xl text-[#25253b]">
            Managing activities and training scores at{" "}
            <strong className="font-bold text-[#10132f]">HCMUS.</strong>
          </p>
        </header>

        <div className="
                    w-full max-w-[630px]
                    rounded-[28px] bg-white
                    px-7 py-7
                    shadow-[0_8px_18px_rgba(0,0,0,0.16)]
                    sm:px-10
                ">
          <h2 className="
                        mb-3 text-3xl font-bold
                        tracking-tight text-[#10132f]
                    ">
            Sign In
          </h2>

          <LoginForm redirectTo={redirectTo} />
        </div>
      </section>
    </main>
  );
}

export default LoginPage;

 # PROGRESS ΓÇö Public Landing Page
 
 Last updated: 2026-11-13  
 Branch: `fix/frontend/refine-homepage`  
 Client root: `src/client`  
 Feature: `specs/001-landing-page`  
 Working tree: intentionally uncommitted; no commit was created.
 
 ## Current Task and Overall Objective
 
 Implement the myHCMUS public Landing Page at `/` from:
 - `specs/001-landing-page/spec.md`
 - `specs/001-landing-page/plan.md`
 - `specs/001-landing-page/tasks.md`
 - `.specify/memory/constitution.md`
 - `docs/ui/landing-page-ui.png`
 
 The feature is frontend-only. Mock activity/auth modes are the default. No backend, API-route, or proxy behavior was changed.
 
 All automated implementation and verification work is complete. Remaining tasks are manual browser/visual/accessibility checks and product-content decisions that cannot be resolved from the repository.
 
 ## Completed Work
 
 ### Foundation
 - Added Vitest tooling and scripts in `package.json`.
 - Added `vitest.config.ts`, `tests/setup.ts`, and `tests/test-utils.tsx`.
 - Added shared `SectionId`, `NavigationLink`, and `FooterContent` types.
 - Removed the Node-only `http` import from `api-client.ts`; `api.get` now forwards `RequestInit` options including `AbortSignal`.
 - Added landing design tokens and light-only base styling in `globals.css`.
 - Wired the existing Geist fonts and removed the stale unused `Metadata` import.
 - Implemented `formatActivityTime` with `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` formatting.
 - Implemented `getDashboardPath`, `getLoginHref`, and `isSafeRedirectPath`.
 - Added `service-mode.ts`.
 - Fixed stale `AuthProvider` memoization and removed unused imports.
 - Added mock auth QA scenarios: `guest | student | organizer | admin`, defaulting to `student`.
 - Added local landing images and four local service icons.
 
 ### Shared UI and Chrome
 - Added Button, Container, Section, SectionHeader, Badge, Tag, Skeleton, EmptyState, ErrorState, and SurfaceCard.
 - Added ArrowRight, Calendar, Location, Lock, Menu, and Close icons.
 - Added Logo, CopyrightYear, SiteHeader, and SiteFooter.
 - Removed the unused `SectionHeaderSpacer`; section spacing is now handled by section wrappers.
 
 ### Landing and Activities
 - Added all landing config modules: nav, sections, hero, highlights, guides, footer, services, and SEO.
 - Centralized remaining user-facing copy in config: service access/external-link/unavailable labels and the guide unavailable label.
 - Added Hero, Highlights, Services, Help, and Footer composition.
 - Added the public route at `src/app/(public)/page.tsx`.
 - Added `src/features/landing/metadata.ts` as the public metadata entrypoint so the route does not import feature internals.
 - Removed the conflicting old `src/app/page.tsx`.
 - Implemented activity DTO/domain types, mapper, fixtures, real/mock services, factory, and hook.

 - **Phase 7 (US5)**: Depends on US1 header/hero and Phase 1 navigation helpers; can run in parallel with US2/US3/US4 after US1.
 - **Phase 8**: Depends on all desired user stories.
 - **Phase 9**: Depends on Phase 8.
 
 ### User Story Dependencies
 
 - **US1 (P1)**: No dependency on other stories; MVP.
 - **US2 (P2)**: Uses US1 activity types and success path; independently testable across outcomes.
 - **US3 (P3)**: Uses US1 services shell and shared auth state; independently testable for gating.
 - **US4 (P4)**: Uses US1 header/hero/services and shared auth state; independently testable for roles.
 - **US5 (P5)**: Uses US1 header/hero; independently testable for navigation.

 - Write the listed tests first and confirm the expected failure before implementation.
 - Types and config before services/components.
 - Services and mappers before hooks.
 - Primitive cards before grids/sections.
 - Integrate only through public feature barrels.
 - Do not modify backend code, API routes, or the proxy for this feature.

 - US5 tests T084-T085 are parallel; scroll utilities and login redirect can be developed alongside header work once tests exist.
 - Phase 8 checks T095-T102 are independent verification tasks and can be assigned to different reviewers.

parts.text:
FR-066 explicitly hero headline contrast. Current gold fails. Need fix to meet spec. We must change hero headline to accessible color. Could use a darker gold for text on light background. But the reference visual is gold; a darker gold (#a16207) still gold/brown. Could maybe increase contrast by changing overlay to dark on left? But FR-066 says hero headline over campus visual; design reference gold on light. A darker gold is appropriate. SC-011 says all confirmed interface text passes. "Confirmed" text; hero headline text is confirmed? Wording pending only Grown vs Grow, but text present. We should make it pass.

Which token? `--color-accent-gold: #f2b31b` used for h1 and logo "my". Logo is also text on white and likely fails (incomplete). Could introduce `--color-accent-gold-strong` or change accent-gold to darker. But the design uses gold for logo/h1. Changing to #a16207 makes logo dark amber. Maybe acceptable accessible compromise. Could use separate `--color-accent-gold-text: #8a5a00` for text on light surfaces; keep `--color-accent-gold` for decorative accents (e.g., focus ring, maybe not text). Search usages.

# Quickstart: Public Landing Page

**Feature**: `001-landing-page` | **Date**: 2026-11-13

This guide is for implementation and verification of the landing page. It assumes the feature plan has been implemented. It does not replace the specification or the contracts.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js compatible with the project's Next.js 16 setup.
- Dependencies installed from the repository root of the client app.
- Read `AGENTS.md` before changing Next.js code. This project uses Next.js 16 conventions (`proxy.ts`, `preload` instead of `priority`).
- Do not commit secrets or a real backend URL in `.env.local`.

## Install and Run

From `src/client`:

```powershell
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

Quality gates:

```powershell
npm run lint
npm run build
npm test
```

`npm test` is available after the test-tooling task adds Vitest and the test scripts. Until then, use `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, and run the manual checks below.

## Mock Configuration

Create an untracked `.env.local` for local verification:

```dotenv
NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=mock
NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_ACTIVITY_SCENARIO=success
NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH_STATE=student
```

| Variable | Values | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE` | `mock` (default), `api` | Selects the activity service implementation |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_ACTIVITY_SCENARIO` | `success`, `partial`, `empty`, `error`, `delay`, `single-list`, `all-invalid`, `long-content` | Selects deterministic activity fixtures |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH_STATE` | `guest`, `student`, `organizer`, `admin` | Optional mock-auth QA scenario; default preserves the existing signed-in mock behavior |

`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are embedded at build time. Restart the dev server after changing them.

### Real service configuration

When the backend contract is confirmed:

```dotenv
NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=api
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=https://your-confirmed-api.example
```

Do not enable this until the endpoint, response envelope, field names, and image host are confirmed. If activity images are remote, add the confirmed host to `images.remotePatterns`; do not use a broad allowlist.

## Verification Matrix

### 1. Static page and composition

1. Open `/` with activities in `delay` mode.
2. Confirm the header, hero, highlights, help, and footer render before the activity request completes.
3. Confirm there is exactly one `h1`, section titles are `h2`, and card titles are `h3`.
4. Confirm the six sections appear in order: Hero, Highlights, Activities, Services, Help, Footer.
5. Confirm the page metadata title, description, and social preview are present.
6. Confirm the footer copyright year matches the current year and is not a hardcoded value.

### 2. Guest behavior

1. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH_STATE=guest`.
2. Confirm the header shows Log In and reserves its space without a Dashboard flash.
3. Confirm Get Started opens `/login` and, after successful sign-in, lands on the role dashboard.
4. Confirm header Log In from the services area returns to `/#services` after sign-in.
5. Confirm public services are usable and authenticated-only services are blurred, inert, unselectable, and absent from the accessibility tree.
6. Confirm there is no ∩┐╜?oLog in to see all services∩┐╜?? overlay.

### 3. Signed-in behavior

1. Set the mock auth state to `student`, then repeat for `organizer` and `admin`.
2. Confirm `/` does not redirect away.
3. Confirm the header shows Dashboard and links to the correct role dashboard.
4. Confirm all services are visible and usable.
5. Confirm Get Started goes directly to the role dashboard.

### 4. Activity states

Use the mock scenario variable and reload `/` for each case:

| Scenario | Expected |
|----------|----------|
| `success` | Two featured cards on the left and three compact cards on the right on wide screens |
| `partial` | Invalid records are omitted; valid records still render |
| `empty` | Empty message with reserved height; no empty grid |
| `error` | Error message and Try again; the rest of the page remains usable |
| `delay` | Skeleton persists; header and other sections remain usable |
| `single-list` | Up to five featured-style cards, at most three columns |
| `all-invalid` | Error outcome; no broken cards |
| `long-content` | Four-line featured title clamp, three-line compact clamp, multi-day date, missing optional fields omitted, image fallback |

Retry:

1. Start in `error`.
2. Activate Try again repeatedly.
3. Confirm the section enters loading and ends in exactly one success, empty, or error outcome with no duplicate content.

### 5. Navigation

1. Click each header link; confirm the section lands below the floating header and the URL hash updates.
2. Scroll through the page; confirm the active link updates and uses more than color.
3. Open `/#services` directly; confirm the services section is positioned correctly after images/fonts finish loading.
4. Use browser Back and Forward; confirm the previous/next section is restored.
5. Open the brand; confirm it returns to the top.

### 6. Mobile drawer

Use a viewport below 1024px:

1. Open the menu; confirm it is modal, contains all section links and the auth action, and locks page scrolling.
2. Press Tab repeatedly; confirm focus stays inside the drawer.
3. Press Escape; confirm the drawer closes and focus returns to the menu trigger.
4. Activate the backdrop; confirm the drawer closes and focus returns to the trigger.
5. Select a section; confirm the drawer closes and the page moves to that section.

### 7. Responsive layout

Check at 320, 375, 640, 768, 1024, 1440, and 1920 pixels wide.

- 320∩┐╜?"639: one column for highlights, services, and guides; hero actions stack; compact activities stay horizontal.
- 640∩┐╜?"1023: header uses the menu; highlights and services use two columns; guides use two columns; featured activities use two columns; compact activities form a two-column stack below.
- 1024+: three highlight columns; 3x2 services; 2x2 guides; featured/compact activity arrangement as designed.
- No horizontal scrolling at any width.
- Touch targets are at least 44x44px.

### 8. Accessibility

1. Navigate the entire page by keyboard; every interactive element is reachable in a logical order with visible focus.
2. Confirm the activity section announces loading/empty/error without moving focus.
3. Confirm status labels include text and are not color-only.
4. Confirm decorative images/shapes are hidden and content images have meaningful alternatives.
5. Confirm the mobile drawer excludes the rest of the page from keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
6. Enable reduced motion; confirm scrolling is immediate, hover lift is suppressed, and skeleton pulse is disabled.
7. Run `axe-core` checks (once the test helper exists) and review the report for critical violations.
8. Check text contrast at WCAG 2.1 AA, especially the hero headline over the campus image and white text on the deep-blue services/footer backgrounds.

### 9. Images and resilience

1. Force the hero image to fail; confirm the layout remains intact and the text stays readable.
2. Force an activity image to fail; confirm the branded placeholder preserves card dimensions.
3. Use an invalid image URL in a mock fixture; confirm no layout shift.
4. Throttle the network; confirm the activity skeleton does not block the rest of the page.

### 10. Activity contract edge cases

1. A single ordered list is treated as upcoming and rendered in the featured style.
2. A single list after grouped placeholders may reflow without clipping, overlap, or horizontal scrolling.
3. An activity with no categories or location omits those lines without punctuation artifacts.
4. A multi-day activity displays both dates and times in `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`.
5. A title with Vietnamese text renders exactly as supplied, with no case transformation.
6. Extra featured/upcoming items are ignored beyond the display caps.

## Automated Test Targets

Once the test tooling is installed:

```powershell
npm test
npm run test:watch
```

Expected coverage:

- `formatActivityTime` timezone, same-day, multi-day, midnight, and invalid input.
- `getDashboardPath`, `getLoginHref`, and safe redirect validation, including open-redirect rejection.
- `activity.mapper` grouped/single-list shapes, invalid-item skipping, all-invalid errors, caps, href encoding, and title preservation.
- Real/mock activity service contract, API path/signal use, and error propagation.
- `useLandingActivities` loading/success/empty/error, retry, abort, stale-response protection, and mapper-error handling.
- `ActivitiesSection` state rendering, retry, and announcements.
- `ActivityGrid` layout rules.
- `ActivityCard` links, clamps, optional fields, image fallback, and status text.
- `HeroActions` guest/authenticated/loading targets.
- `ServicesSection` guest/authenticated/loading gating.
- `SiteHeader` auth actions, role dashboard path, mobile dialog, and active section.
- `GuideCard` available/unavailable destinations.
- `axe-core` checks for key client renders.

## Known Limitations and Release Dependencies

- The activity endpoint, envelope, and field names are provisional. Do not enable the real service until the backend confirms them.
- The real media host is unknown; remote activity images require a confirmed image allowlist.
- Two service names/icons, final hero wording, help destinations, and footer copy are pending.
- `/help` may not exist; guide cards whose destinations are unavailable must render as unavailable, not dead links.
- The existing auth mock auto-authenticates a test student. Guest-state manual QA depends on the optional mock-auth scenario; otherwise use component tests and the real backend.
- The existing proxy has an unrelated authenticated-`/login` redirect issue; avoid expanding this feature into a proxy refactor.
- Next.js 16 uses `preload`, not `priority`, for the hero image.
- Do not add a new runtime dependency for this feature; test dependencies are dev-only and justified in the plan.

1. Navigate the entire page by keyboard; every interactive element is reachable in a logical order with visible focus.
2. Confirm the activity section announces loading/empty/error without moving focus.
3. Confirm status labels include text and are not color-only.
4. Confirm decorative images/shapes are hidden and content images have meaningful alternatives.

6. Enable reduced motion; confirm scrolling is immediate, hover lift is suppressed, and skeleton pulse is disabled.

1. Force the hero image to fail; confirm the layout remains intact and the text stays readable.
2. Force an activity image to fail; confirm the branded placeholder preserves card dimensions.
3. Use an invalid image URL in a mock fixture; confirm no layout shift.
4. Throttle the network; confirm the activity skeleton does not block the rest of the page.

### 10. Activity contract edge cases

1. A single ordered list is treated as upcoming and rendered in the featured style.
2. A single list after grouped placeholders may reflow without clipping, overlap, or horizontal scrolling.
3. An activity with no categories or location omits those lines without punctuation artifacts.
4. A multi-day activity displays both dates and times in `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`.
5. A title with Vietnamese text renders exactly as supplied, with no case transformation.
6. Extra featured/upcoming items are ignored beyond the display caps.

 ## Dependencies and Execution Order
 
 ### Phase Dependencies
 
 - **Phase 1**: No dependencies; start immediately.
 - **Phase 2**: Depends on Phase 1 tokens/types; blocks landing composition.
 - **Phase 3 (US1)**: Depends on Phase 1 and Phase 2; delivers the MVP shell, grouped activity success, and all six section shells.
 - **Phase 4 (US2)**: Depends on US1 activity types/services; can begin once the US1 activity success path exists.
 - **Phase 5 (US3)**: Depends on US1 services shell and Phase 1 auth memo fix; can run in parallel with US2 if staffed.
 - **Phase 6 (US4)**: Depends on US1 header/hero/services and Phase 1 navigation helpers; can run in parallel with US2/US3 after US1.
 - **Phase 7 (US5)**: Depends on US1 header/hero and Phase 1 navigation helpers; can run in parallel with US2/US3/US4 after US1.
 - **Phase 8**: Depends on all desired user stories.
 - **Phase 9**: Depends on Phase 8.
 
 ### User Story Dependencies
 
 - **US1 (P1)**: No dependency on other stories; MVP.
 - **US2 (P2)**: Uses US1 activity types and success path; independently testable across outcomes.
 - **US3 (P3)**: Uses US1 services shell and shared auth state; independently testable for gating.
 - **US4 (P4)**: Uses US1 header/hero/services and shared auth state; independently testable for roles.
 - **US5 (P5)**: Uses US1 header/hero; independently testable for navigation.
 
 ### Within Each Story
 
 - Write the listed tests first and confirm the expected failure before implementation.
 - Types and config before services/components.
 - Services and mappers before hooks.
 - Primitive cards before grids/sections.
 - Integrate only through public feature barrels.
 - Do not modify backend code, API routes, or the proxy for this feature.
 
 ### Parallel Opportunities
 
 - Phase 1 test harness tasks T002-T004 are parallel after T001.
 - Phase 1 shared utilities T009-T016 are largely parallel by file, except T010 depends on T009 and T012 depends on T011.
 - Phase 2 primitives T017-T024 are parallel by file.
 - US1 config tasks T028-T030 are parallel; T038 can run alongside them.
 - US1 activity presentation T046-T047 can run in parallel after activity types.
 - US2 tests T051-T056 are parallel; implementation T058, T059, and T062 can run alongside mapper work.
 - US3 tests T069-T070 are parallel; config/icons T071/T074 can run before card/section gating.
 - US4 test tasks T077-T078 are parallel; header/hero/services updates T079-T081 touch different files.
 - US5 tests T084-T085 are parallel; scroll utilities and login redirect can be developed alongside header work once tests exist.
 - Phase 8 checks T095-T102 are independent verification tasks and can be assigned to different reviewers.
 - Phase 9 manual checks T106-T112 can run in parallel by different reviewers, while T103-T105 are sequential quality gates.

## 1. Purpose & Scope

The landing page is the public entry point of **myHCMUS**, a platform for extracurricular activities and student training scores (DRS) at HCMUS.

1. Explain what the platform does (hero + highlights).

## 1. Purpose & Scope

The landing page is the public entry point of **myHCMUS**, a platform for extracurricular activities and student training scores (DRS) at HCMUS.

Goals:
1. Explain what the platform does (hero + highlights).
2. Showcase featured/upcoming activities, fetched from an API, with complete loading / empty / error handling.
3. Give quick access to university services; **guests see only part of them**, the rest is blurred to motivate login.
4. Point to help content and provide contact info (footer).

Out of scope: login form (`/login`), dashboards, the activity detail page, the full activities list page, About Us and Help pages. Only their **links** are wired from here.

---

## 2. Page Anatomy

A global header floats over the hero. The page body has **6 sections**:

| # | Section | Anchor id | Background | Data source |
|---|---------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| 0 | Site Header (global, floating) | ΓÇö | white pill over hero | static nav config + auth state |
| 1 | Hero | `home` | campus photo + white gradient | static |
| 2 | Platform Highlights | `about` | white card overlapping hero | static config |
| 3 | Featured & Upcoming Activities | `activities` | page background (white/very light) | **API** |
| 4 | HCMUS Services (Quick Access) | `services` | full-bleed deep blue | static config + **auth state** |
| 5 | Help / Guide | `help` | white with decorative blue circles | static config |
| 6 | Footer | `contact` | full-bleed deep blue | static config |

Header nav items map to anchors: Home ΓåÆ `#home`, About Us ΓåÆ `#about`, Activities ΓåÆ `#activities`, Services ΓåÆ `#services`, Help ΓåÆ `#help`.

---

## 3. Fit with the Existing Frontend

Existing structure (Next.js App Router): `app/(public)`, `app/(protected)/{admin,organizer,student}`, `features/auth/*` (context, provider, schema, services + mock service, types, DTO), `hooks/useAuth.ts`, `libs/{api-client,navigation,roles,session}.ts`, `components/{forms,icons}`, `types/{api,entities}.ts`.

Follow the same conventions already used by `features/auth`:
- Feature-first folders under `features/<name>/`.
- **Service + mock service** pair behind one interface (see `auth.service.ts` / `mock.auth.service.ts`). Reuse whatever switching mechanism auth uses (env flag or factory) ΓÇö do not invent a second one.
- **DTO vs domain type separation** (`*.dto.ts` = wire format, `*.ts` = UI model) with a mapper.
- One icon per file in `components/icons`.
- HTTP goes through `libs/api-client.ts` only; no raw `fetch` in components.
- Role ΓåÆ dashboard resolution uses `libs/roles.ts` / `libs/navigation.ts`. If a `getDashboardPath(role)` helper does not exist yet, add it there (do not hardcode paths in components).

### 3.1 Routing

- Landing route: **`app/(public)/page.tsx`** ΓåÆ renders `<LandingPage />` from `features/landing`.
- **Remove or empty the current `app/page.tsx`** ΓÇö two files resolving to `/` conflict.
- `app/(public)/layout.tsx` currently serves `/login`; check what it renders. The landing page composes `SiteHeader` / `SiteFooter` itself (inside `LandingPage`) so `/login` is not affected. If more marketing pages appear later, extract a `(site)` route group with a shared layout.
- The landing page is **always accessible**, including for authenticated users (no auto-redirect to dashboard). Authenticated users get a "Dashboard" button in the header and unlocked services.

### 3.2 Rendering strategy

- `app/(public)/page.tsx` is a **Server Component** (static shell, SEO metadata).
- Interactive/stateful parts are Client Components (`"use client"`): `SiteHeader` (auth state, mobile menu, scroll-spy), `ActivitiesSection` (data fetch states), `ServicesSection` (auth gating).
- Activities are fetched **client-side** through a hook so a slow/failed API never blocks the page. [ASSUMPTION] If the project already uses React Query/SWR in `providers/provider.tsx`, use it inside the hook instead of hand-rolled state; the hook's return contract stays the same.

---

## 4. File / Folder Plan

```
app/

```ts

  id: string; name: string; href: string;        // external URL
  icon: { src: string; alt: string };

**Guest vs authenticated behavior (key requirement)**
- **Guest** (`!isAuthenticated`): items with `access: "public"` (first column in the design: Moodle, Student Portal) render normally and are clickable. Items with `access: "authenticated"` render **blurred** ("half visible, half hidden"):
  - CSS `filter: blur(6pxΓÇô8px)` (blur grows slightly toward the right edge in the design: column 2 Γëê light, column 3 Γëê heavier ΓÇö implement with per-column blur or a left-to-right mask; a single uniform blur is acceptable), reduced opacity Γëê `0.85`.
  - `pointer-events: none`, `aria-hidden="true"`, `inert`, `tabIndex={-1}`; text must not be selectable.
  - Optional overlay (recommended, not in the PNG) **[ASSUMPTION]**: a centered pill over the blurred area with `LockIcon` + "Log in to see all services" ΓåÆ `/login` (preserve return target: `/login?redirectTo=/%23services` or whatever convention `libs/navigation.ts` already uses).
- **Authenticated**: all cards fully visible and clickable; blur removed (can animate `filter` over Γëê `300ms` once auth resolves).
- `isLoading`: render the **guest (locked) version** to avoid showing protected cards for a flash; unlock when resolved. DOM structure is identical so there is no layout shift.
- Security note: blur is a UX hint only. Protected URLs are not secrets; if a service must be truly protected it is protected by the target system. Do not render real hrefs for locked cards in guest state (use `href` only when unlocked).
- External links: `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Card hover: slight lift/shadow; focus-visible ring (white on blue).

## 8. User Flows

### 8.1 Guest ΓÇö first visit
1. Lands on `/` ΓåÆ header (Log In), hero, highlights render immediately (static).
2. `ActivitiesSection` mounts ΓåÆ skeleton ΓåÆ API ΓåÆ (success | empty | error) per ┬º7.3.
3. Scrolls to Services: sees Moodle + Student Portal clearly, other cards blurred + (optional) "Log in to see all services".
4. Clicks **Log In** (header / overlay / Get Started) ΓåÆ `/login` (return target preserved). After login, `AuthProvider` sets the user and the app redirects to the role dashboard (existing auth flow) or back to `#services` if `redirectTo` is used.
5. Clicks an activity card ΓåÆ `/activities/{id}` [ASSUMPTION: detail page is publicly viewable; registering requires login].
6. Clicks a guide card ΓåÆ `/help#ΓÇª`.

### 8.2 Authenticated user (student / organizer / admin)
1. Lands on `/` (no forced redirect). Header shows **Dashboard** (+ user menu).
2. Services section is fully unlocked (blur removed).
3. **Get Started** and **Dashboard** ΓåÆ `getDashboardPath(role)` (`/student/dashboard`, `/organizer/dashboard`, `/admin/dashboard`).
4. Activities behave the same as for guests.

### 8.3 Activities API outcomes
- Slow response: skeleton persists (no timeout UI needed; abort on unmount).
- 2xx with data: render per layout rules.
- 2xx with empty lists: empty state (not an error).
- Network/5xx/invalid payload: error state + **Try again** (re-enters `loading`).
- 401/403 must not occur (public endpoint); if it does, treat as `error`.

### 8.4 Navigation
Header link click ΓåÆ smooth scroll to section (accounting for floating header height via `scroll-margin-top`); direct visit to `/#services` scrolls on load; scroll-spy updates active link; browser back works with hashes.

## 9. Non-functional Requirements

- **Accessibility**: semantic landmarks (`header`, `main`, `section[aria-labelledby]`, `footer`); one `h1` (hero headline), section titles `h2`, card titles `h3`; visible focus rings; meaningful `alt` for content images, `alt=""` for decoration; contrast ΓëÑ 4.5:1 (check gold headline over photo ΓÇö keep text-shadow); respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (disable smooth scroll/lift animations); blurred locked cards hidden from assistive tech.
- **Performance**: hero image `priority`; below-fold images lazy; `next/image` with explicit `sizes`; no layout shift (skeletons share dimensions with real cards); activities fetch must not block first paint.
- **SEO**: `metadata` in `app/(public)/page.tsx` (title "myHCMUS ΓÇö Extracurricular activities & training scores", description, OpenGraph image).
- **i18n readiness**: keep all copy in `config/*.ts` and component props rather than inline JSX strings; UI language is English. Activity titles arrive as-is (Vietnamese).
- **Error isolation**: a failure in one section (activities) must never break others; consider a section-level error boundary around `ActivitiesSection`.
- **Testing**: unit-test `formatActivityTime`, `activity.mapper`, `useLandingActivities` (all four states via the mock service), `ServicesSection` (guest vs authenticated rendering), `ActivityGrid` layout rules (1/2 featured ├ù 0/1/3 upcoming).
